core_claim.text: Claude Code has a frontend-design skill that makes AI-built web interfaces stop looking generic, and a user can install it.
core_claim.note: Test fixture for the fake claude (not real research): the skill is listed in the anthropics/skills repository and the docs describe how skills install.

claims.claim: The frontend-design skill is published in the anthropics/skills repository on GitHub
A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file that Claude Code loads when the task matches its description
Skills install by copying the folder into ~/.claude/skills/ or a project's .claude/skills/
The skill steers the model away from the defaults it reaches for: common fonts, purple gradients, centered hero layouts
Anthropic described agent skills, the frontend-design skill among them, in a blog post
A forum thread claims the skill doubles conversion rates
The skill generates whole React apps on its own
claims.note: fixture: it changes design choices, it does not generate apps by itself

pitfalls: Skills need Claude Code 2.0 or newer
A skill only triggers when the task matches the description in its frontmatter
one_true_thing: One folder copied into ~/.claude/skills changes every frontend Claude Code builds
The skill lists the exact defaults it bans: the default font, purple gradients, centered heroes
unverified: How many people use the skill
summary: Fixture summary: the skill exists, installs by copying a folder and changes design defaults. Avoid any conversion claim.
